s1.syndrome_frame: Acute episodic neurological syndrome with abdominal pain and vomiting
salient_findings: Generalized abdominal pain
Vomiting
Diaphoresis, mucocutaneous paleness, dizziness, dysarthria, incoherent speech, and lack of eye contact
Frontal headache and persistent nausea after the episode
Confusion and disorientation on neurologic examination
key_facts: 8-year-old boy with no significant past medical history
30-minute history of generalized abdominal pain
Single episode of vomiting
Developed diaphoresis, mucocutaneous paleness, dizziness, dysarthria, incoherent speech, and lack of eye contact
Episode lasted 10 minutes
Reported frontal headache (5/10) and persistent nausea after the episode
Family denied toxin or medication exposure
Similar episode 18 months earlier, diagnosed as migraine
No personal or family history of epilepsy or neurological disorders
Developmental milestones were age-appropriate
Vital signs were normal except for blood pressure above the 95th percentile for age
Neurologic examination revealed confusion and disorientation
Motor and sensory examinations were normal
Consciousness and orientation improved approximately 20 minutes after arrival
Had three additional self-limited vomiting episodes and ongoing headache
Headache improved after a single IV dose of diclofenac (1 mg/kg)
Complete blood count, serum chemistries, and electrolytes were all within normal limits
Brain MRI with an epilepsy protocol was reported as normal for age

shortlist.label: Migraine with abdominal aura
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of similar episodes diagnosed as migraine and presents with abdominal pain, vomiting, and headache

shortlist.label: Cyclic vomiting syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient experiences recurrent episodes of vomiting and abdominal pain, consistent with cyclic vomiting syndrome

shortlist.label: Abdominal epilepsy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's episodes of abdominal pain, vomiting, and altered mental status could be indicative of abdominal epilepsy

shortlist.label: Familial hemiplegic migraine
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms, including headache, vomiting, and transient neurological deficits, are consistent with familial hemiplegic migraine

shortlist.label: Basilar migraine
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms, including headache, vomiting, and transient neurological deficits, could be indicative of basilar migraine

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including generalized abdominal pain, vomiting, diaphoresis, and headache, are consistent with migraine with abdominal aura. The episode's duration and the patient's previous similar episode diagnosed as migraine also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cyclic vomiting syndrome
rejected.why: Lack of recurrent, severe vomiting episodes at regular intervals

rejected.label: Abdominal epilepsy
rejected.why: Normal brain MRI and no personal or family history of epilepsy

rejected.label: Familial hemiplegic migraine
rejected.why: No family history of hemiplegic migraine and no hemiparesis during episodes

rejected.label: Basilar migraine
rejected.why: No symptoms suggestive of brainstem involvement, such as visual field defects or ataxia
